own_solution.law: Double Doppler: f_rec = f (c - w)(c - v) / (c (c + w)); shift = f - f_rec

notes: Agrees with pass 1. The authors' relations (w = lorry speed, v = trolley speed) give the same product as mine. Checked R answers: recorder ground speed 10.1 m/s gives 1500*337*332.9/119707 = 1405.774 Hz, shift 94.226 Hz; 10.6 m/s gives 96.338 Hz; 11.4 m/s gives 1500*337*331.6/119707 = 1400.284 Hz, shift 99.716 Hz. The crest-timing cancellation relations are correct: t_h = (q + c t)/(c - w), T = (q + (c + w) t_h)/(c - v), and the difference T_(n+1) - T_n = (c + w)/(f (c - w)) * c/(c - v)... i.e. independent of q, inverse reproduces f (c - w)(c - v)/(c (c + w)). Minimal pairs T02E2/TBF04 (earlier run vs this run) and T4BE2/TA0C8 (toolbox vs recorder) all state 1.6 m/s and differ only in attachment. Numeral-free twins match wording.
